summary.name: ExifCleaner
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source app that strips EXIF and other metadata from photos, videos, and PDFs via drag and drop.
use_cases: Removing location data from photos before sharing online
Batch-stripping metadata from many images or videos
Cleaning PDFs of hidden metadata before publishing
Checking what metadata a file contains before removal
Preserving image orientation while removing other EXIF fields
summary.what_it_does: ExifCleaner removes metadata from images, videos, and PDFs, including formats such as JPEG, PNG, WebP, TIFF, GIF, MP4, MOV, M4A, and PDF. Users drag files or folders onto the window and metadata is stripped. It can process large batches of files at once. Expanding a file shows a before-and-after diff of the removed metadata fields. Options let users preserve orientation, save copies instead of overwriting, and strip extended attributes. The page says it has no network access and no telemetry, and that its source code is open for verification.
notable: Open source, so privacy claims (no network access, no telemetry) can be checked in the code
Before-and-after diff of removed metadata fields for each file
Batch processing of hundreds or thousands of files via drag and drop
Available in 24+ languages and follows the OS light or dark theme
caveats: The page does not state a platform list beyond what testimonials imply; Linux and other platforms are not mentioned
One testimonial mentions the app is built with Electron, which the page itself does not state
